unsupported_codes.reason: Keratitis, the category that holds the corneal ulcer codes: reporting one treats the ulcer as a current condition, and the note documents it as resolved after completed treatment.

citations.Z09: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY2027, Section I.C.21.c.8: follow-up codes explain continuing surveillance following completed treatment and imply that the condition has been fully treated and no longer exists; the follow-up code is sequenced first, followed by the history code. Section IV.J: conditions that were previously treated and no longer exist are not coded. Here the corneal ulcer is documented as resolved after completed treatment and the cornea is clear, so the visit is reported as a follow-up examination and the ulcer is not reported.
citations.Z86.69: Tabular List instruction at Z09: use additional code to identify any applicable history of disease code (Z86.-, Z87.-); instruction at Z86: code first any follow-up examination after treatment (Z09). ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY2027, Section I.B.7: a 'use additional code' note indicates that a secondary code should be added, if known. The inclusion term at Z86.6 is 'Conditions classifiable to G00-G99, H00-H95', and the subcategory has no code more specific to the eye than Z86.69. Here the treated condition is a corneal ulcer, an eye condition, so Z86.69 is reported after Z09.

coder_notes: The history code is required, not optional. Section I.C.21.c.8 says only that follow-up codes may be used with history codes, but the Tabular List instruction at Z09 applies, and Section I of the guidelines says that the conventions and instructions of the classification take precedence over guidelines. No long-term drug therapy code: the eye drops were finished a week before the visit.
